title: Ma Rainey, Chicago bands and the Jarland Park job
summary: He swapped jobs with trombonist Lewis Taylor, nearly went west with Les Hite's band, and was up for a place in Richard Jones's band at Jarland Park.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Tell me, when did you change over to right handed trombone then?

Oh I had been playing quite a few years. And how that come about, oh I had worked with Maureen and been all over the country and everything. And so I changed places with, I got tired of traveling. And there was another fellow here, a trombone artist, Lewis Taylor, he had never been out of Chicago. And he was with a very good band, a very good dance band. Let's see, what was the name of his band. I can't tell. But anyway, it was a very good outfit and the outfit was fellows like Les Hyde, Lionel Hampton, I don't know. They were all youngsters all the way up. But it was, so he had never been in a place, I say suppose we changed jobs. So we did. He went with Maureen and I went with them. So this band worked for a while until Les and Arnoldoff, George Arnoldoff and some of the boys got this chance to go to the coast. Well I had an offer to go along with them, one of those things, but my mother wouldn't let me go. She said no I don't want you going that far. So then I stayed around here. So there was a, Richard Jones was getting a band to go in a place on 33rd and Wabash. It was an amusement park with a dance pavilion, one of those diamond dance deals. And so he was getting this band. And it was just one of those things that was almost set for me. He had taken two or three of the boys that we'd come up with, Gabriel Washington, the drummer, and whatnot. The place was there, it was called Jarland Park. Of course the native Chicago's had another name for it, but we won't go into that.
You don't want to get that on the tape. Yeah.
